content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies robustness to distribution shift of RF localization. It includes 8 localiser nets on 5 RF localization datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- This paper provides an experimental analysis of learning and distribution shift of RF localization.
- It does well support its own points.
- It is well written and easy to follow.

Weakness
- This paper provides comprehensive analysis of distribution shift in RF localization domain. However, there is no novel idea proposed, the findings/practical tips are trivial, and the contribution to ML community is marginal.
- Compared to the findings, proposing robust method against distribution shift in RF might be more interesting. There are many great methods in literature, I would recommend to compare those and identify the most suitable one and understand why it works the best on such a real-life application sounds more promising.
- This is an experimental-driven paper, however, some experiment details might be missing, e.g.,
   a) how the authors separate train, val, test sets?
   b) in figure 2-4, are these loss/error on train or test sets?
   c) as TAoA2Pos the upperbound, why CSI2POS achieves better (again, train or test) loss? If train loss, is the model overfitting?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper does well support its own points and easy to follow, yet with no novel idea proposed.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper focus on an experimental exploration of distribution shift in RF localization. RF-domain conferences/journals might be a better match.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper is about localization using radio-frequency signals such as WiFi or 5G. The authors propose a study on how different algorithms from literature perform in different environments and how they perforn in out-of-distribution scenarios.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
It is not clearly stated whether the authors intend to release their 5 datasets. What does industry-grade mean? Is this measured data or simulated data?

Eq (1): The equation seems odd. $\Sigma_m$ is 3x3. A is defined as the angle of arrival matrix - what are its dimensions and what are its entries? Since $u_m$ is a 3-vector, then $r$ must be a vector - what are its entries? $r$ is stated to contain time of arrivals - is this a calibrated setting in which the exact transmission times are known? How are direct connections between devices distinguished from indirect connections, ie connections whose paths are reflected from some objects?

Eq (2) (channel impulse response): Why is this a model for a single antenna although multiple antennas are assumed in Eq (1)?

The main weak points of this paper, in my opinion are the lack of novel contributions since the authors only evaluated existing models on their new data, so there is not much to be learned from this paper.
content.summary_of_the_review: The lack of technical novelty. Since this is an experimental paper, I cannot evaluate the correctness of the claims made here.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In order to characterize and compare how learnt localizer networks can be deployed in the field under real-world radio frequency distribution shifts, this manuscript developed the RadioBench that is composed of eight SOTA learnt localizer nets on five novel industry-grade datasets. Conclusions and recommendations based on the performance measurements in terms of (i) learning, (ii) proneness to distribution shift and (iii) localization have been drawn for the deployability in practice.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
1. Comprehensive exploration on characterising and comparing how learnt localizer networks can be deployed in the field under real-world radio frequency distribution shifts.
2. Conclusions and recommendations for practical deployment have been drawn through solid experiments.

Cons:
1. Except for the straightforward description of comparison results, the connections and differences between studied localizer nets are suggested to be analyzed and clarified through numerical experiments.
2. There are some typos in this manuscript. Please check through the whole content carefully.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: It is appreciated that such a comprehensive and insightful comparison study could be conducted, and the recommendations are believed to be helpful for the community.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper presents a solid comparison study to offer insights and recommendations for practical deployment of existing localizer nets, with the depth of analysis however should be enhanced.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
